root_causes.description: An HTTP-boundary abort fault on the payment service causes checkout's outbound call to payment to never complete normally, so checkout blocks until its 10s deadline. Because the abort occurs at the HTTP boundary, payment emits no completed/errored server span, leaving its own server-side latency and error metrics normal (p99≈5ms, error_rate=0).

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000ms, p50=10000ms, mean=9161.7ms, max=10000ms across the window
request_rate mean=0.010, mostly 0 (payment server spans essentially absent)
[no traces found] — aborted client spans not recorded
evidence.expected_baseline: long checkout traces present when latency is real

root_causes.description: Checkout exhibits a severe p99 latency spike pinned at its 10s deadline, but this is a downstream symptom of the payment abort rather than a local fault, since checkout's own error_rate is 0 and there is no local resource pressure.

Checkout's dependency call path through payment is failing/timing out, which is the mechanism of the incident; however the root fault injection is scoped to the payment HTTP boundary rather than checkout itself.

remediation_steps: Disable / roll back the flagd flag injecting the http_abort fault on the payment service to restore normal HTTP responses.
Restart the payment deployment pods to clear any stuck/aborted connection state.
Verify checkout p99 latency returns below 100ms and payment inbound request_rate recovers to its normal steady level.
